findings.source_passage: Certainly Mr. Brown's organization was a far-reaching concern. The common criminal, the well-bred Irish gentleman, the pale Russian, and the efficient German master of the ceremonies! Truly a strange and sinister gathering! Who was this man who held in his finger these curiously variegated links of an unknown chain?
findings.source_locator: After the Irish Sinn Feiner's arrival, before 'In this case, the procedure was exactly the same'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a narratorial aside that establishes the thematic scope of Mr. Brown's coalition and poses the central mystery of his identity; it is stylistically distinctive ('held in his finger these curiously variegated links') and carries interpretive weight for the Brown revelation arc.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the passage verbatim or near-verbatim as a brief narratorial comment after the Sinn Feiner's admission—its rhetorical questions and catalogue of types are signature Christie voice and must not be silently omitted.

findings.source_passage: He was no more fanciful than the majority of young Englishmen, but he could not rid himself of the impression that some unusually potent force emanated from the man. The creature reminded him of a venomous snake.
findings.source_locator: Description of the small pale last-comer, after 'Tommy could hardly believe that the man did not know he was there'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'venomous snake' simile and the qualification 'no more fanciful than the majority of young Englishmen' are voice-defining—they establish both Tommy's character and the sinister quality of Number One in a rhetorically distinctive way that the draft's bare 'Tommy shivered' entirely erases.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinstate the two sentences beginning 'He was no more fanciful…' and 'The creature reminded him of a venomous snake.' These are the signature characterisation notes for Number One's first appearance.

findings.source_passage: "But all the same, it is possible that he is among us now...." He looked round him again, and again that expression of fear swept over the group. Each man seemed eyeing his neighbour doubtfully.
findings.source_locator: Number One's speech about Mr. Brown possibly being present, before 'The Russian tapped his cheek'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft adds 'We never know. We look at each other—one of us is Mr. Brown—which?' which is not in the source and misrepresents Number One's voice; simultaneously the source's detail 'Each man seemed eyeing his neighbour doubtfully' and 'The Russian tapped his cheek' are dropped, erasing the visual/gestural signature of this key interpretive moment about Brown's hidden identity.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the invented dialogue and restore the source's stage direction: 'Each man seemed eyeing his neighbour doubtfully' and 'The Russian tapped his cheek. "So be it."' These details carry significant interpretive weight for the Brown mystery.

findings.source_passage: There was a certain bulldog tenacity about Tommy that made him slow to admit defeat. Checkmated for the moment, he was far from abandoning the conflict. He still intended to hear what was going on in the locked room. As one plan had failed, he must hunt about for another.
findings.source_locator: After Tommy discovers the door is locked, before 'He looked round him'
findings.why_it_matters: This passage is character-defining for Tommy—the 'bulldog tenacity' phrase is a recurring motif in the novel and establishes his particular brand of dogged courage; its complete omission flattens the characterisation in a non-cut passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'bulldog tenacity' passage or at minimum the key sentence 'There was a certain bulldog tenacity about Tommy that made him slow to admit defeat' to preserve the character motif.

findings.source_passage: "Well, I'm damned!" he said. "What a dirty trick!" As his indignation cooled, he prepared to face the situation.
findings.source_locator: After Tommy discovers the door is locked
findings.why_it_matters: Tommy's exclamation is a minor but characteristic voice beat—his ironic good humour in the face of setbacks is a register marker; its omission contributes to the overall flattening of his voice in this section.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the brief exclamation—it takes four words and preserves Tommy's characteristic register.

summary: The draft faithfully reproduces most of the plot and dialogue but erases four signature voice passages—the narratorial aside on Mr. Brown's coalition, the 'venomous snake' characterisation of Number One, the 'bulldog tenacity' character beat for Tommy, and the stage directions confirming mutual fear at the 'among us now' moment—and introduces invented dialogue not in the source; three medium-severity findings trigger regeneration.
